newsitem.title: TURKEY: Jailed Turkish editor to pursue free press drive.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Turkish editor to pursue free press drive.

text.p: A Turkish editor serving a 15-year sentence for his newspaper's stance on the Kurdish issue pledged on Monday to pursue his crusade for press freedom, Anatolian news agency said.
Ocak Isik Yurtcu was quoted as telling reporters at Istanbul University Hospital, where he was taken for a heart checkup, that he was feeling fine.
He said he would press on with his campaign for freedom for all those imprisoned for what they had written, Anatolian reported.
Last week Yurtcu received an award from the U.S.-based Committee to Protect Journalists for his fight for freedom of the press in Turkey.
He was jailed in 1994 for a series of articles about the Kurdish guerrilla campaign in southeast Turkey which appeared in the pro-Kurdish daily Ozgur Gundem.
Yurtcu was the paper's "responsible editor", managing the reporting staff and legally responsible for articles printed.
New Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz has promised to introduce legal measures to secure the release of editors imprisoned on political charges.
President Suleyman Demirel is able to grant amnesty to prisoners on grounds of old age or ill health, but not simply at his discretion.
